findings.title: appStore entries are now unresolved Promises, but callers still use them synchronously in places
findings.body: The appStore object now maps each key to a dynamic import() Promise instead of a module namespace. Any consumer that accesses `appStore[x].lib` (or `"lib" in appStore[x]`) without awaiting gets a Promise, so the `"lib" in app` check is always false and the feature silently behaves as unimplemented. Call sites not updated in this PR (e.g. other usages across the repo beyond the 12 files, such as getApps/utils or payment/locations code that reads appStore synchronously) will break silently rather than fail loudly.

findings.title: Mapping to import() promises changes the module type contract for all importers
findings.body: Previously the default export was a map of module namespaces; now every property is Promise<module>. Any type-level consumer expecting the namespace shape will fail type checking or, if using `as`/casts, fail at runtime. The PR does not show a single shared type or helper (e.g. a typed async accessor) to enforce awaiting, so future callers will easily make the same mistake.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials calls async getCalendar without awaiting, yielding Promise objects as calendars
findings.body: getCalendar is now async, but getCalendarCredentials still does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` and stores the Promise in the returned object. Downstream code in getConnectedCalendars then does `await item.calendar`, which works only by accident, but any other consumer of getCalendarCredentials reading `.calendar` synchronously will get a Promise and treat it as a non-null Calendar, calling methods on it and failing.

findings.title: getCachedResults relies on index alignment that is fine, but a rejected getCalendar aborts all calendars
findings.body: `Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(getCalendar))` now rejects if any single app import fails (e.g. a missing module), causing the whole busy-times lookup to fail, where previously only the failing calendar was affected. This is a behavioral regression for availability computation.

findings.title: forEach with async callback discards promises; deletions run unawaited and errors become unhandled rejections
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` does not await the async callbacks, so the surrounding try/catch never catches errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent. Those rejections become unhandled promise rejections, and the reschedule returns before calendar cleanup finishes. The same pattern is repeated in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, trpc bookings.tsx, and handleCancelBooking.ts (recurring branch).

findings.title: Recurring-cancel calendar deletions run in an un-awaited forEach async callback
findings.body: `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... await calendar?.deleteEvent ... apiDeletes.push(...) })` pushes into apiDeletes after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already captured the array, so these deletions are neither awaited nor have their errors surfaced; the booking can be reported cancelled while calendar events remain, and rejections are unhandled.

findings.title: getVideoAdapters now awaits each app sequentially, serializing imports
findings.body: The for-loop with `await appStore[...]` per credential serializes module loading and adapter creation. This is a latency regression for getBusyVideoTimes and createMeeting with multiple credentials compared to the previous synchronous reduce; Promise.all over the credentials would preserve ordering-insensitive concurrency.

findings.title: updateMeeting does not handle getVideoAdapters failure; createMeeting error path also changed
findings.body: getVideoAdapters now can reject (dynamic import failure). In updateMeeting the call is outside any try/catch, so an import failure throws out of the update flow instead of being reported as success=false. In createMeeting it is also outside the try block, bypassing the sendBrokenIntegrationEmail/calVideo fallback.

findings.title: await used inside a non-async callback context
findings.body: The diff adds `await getCalendar(...)` inside the reference-deletion loop, but the enclosing callback is not shown as async in this hunk; if it is a non-async forEach/map callback the code will not compile or will leave the await effectively unhandled. Verify the surrounding function is async and the loop is a for...of.

findings.title: Payment app lookup returns null from a mutation path after a warn, but the function signature expects a result
findings.body: In the confirm mutation, when the payment app is not implemented the code returns null from inside the handler, skipping refund and status updates while the booking is still treated as rejected by the caller flow; the awaited appStore change does not alter this, but it reinforces that the missing-module case (now a possible import rejection) is not handled at all here.
